title: Celsus and Arnobius’s opponents: statues are dedications and social bridles, not gods with sense
source_text: XLVIII. Id saepius Protestatur Celsus apud Origenem praecipue lib. 7. Ubi postquam dixit ridiculam esse sapientiam, si quis contemnat statuas, ideo quod lapis, aut lignum, aut aes, aut aurum, ab hoc vel illo expolita, non sit Deus, subjungit: Quis enim alius, nisi sit totus fatuus, has Deos credit, non Diis dedicatas statuas? Et similiter, Arnobio teste lib. 6. adversus Gentes, illud dicere simulachrorum assertores solebant, Non ignorasse antiquos nihil habere numinis signa, neque ullum omnino inesse his sensum; sed propter indomitum atque imperitum vulgus, salutariter ea consilioque formasse, ut velut quadam specie objecta his numinum, abjicerent asperitatem metu; arbitratique praesentibus sese sub Diis agere, facta impia deponerent, & ad humana officia, morum immutatione transirent.
pass_a_gloss: That Celsus often protests in Origen especially book 7. Where after he has said that wisdom is ridiculous, if anyone despises statues, because stone, or wood, or bronze, or gold, polished by this or that man, is not God, he subjoins: For who else, unless he be wholly foolish, believes these to be Gods, not statues dedicated to the Gods? And likewise, Arnobius witnessing in book 6 against the Gentiles, the assertors of simulacra were accustomed to say that, that the ancients were not ignorant that signs have nothing of divinity, nor that any sense at all is in them; but that for the sake of the untamed and unskilled crowd they had formed them salutarily and by counsel, that as by a certain species of divinities cast before these, they might cast away harshness by fear; and reckoning that they were acting under Gods present, they might lay down impious deeds, and pass over to human duties by a change of manners.
pass_b_english: Celsus: only a fool thinks the polished metal is God—statues are dedications to gods.
Arnobius’s pagan spokesmen: ancients knew signs lack sense; images bridle the crowd toward civil virtue under felt divine presence.

lemmas.gloss: that signs have nothing of divinity
